## 1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

- **Underlying subscription MRR is growing, but headline October revenue is distorted.** September subscription MRR was **€746.1k**. October MRR was **€757.7k**, up **+€11.6k / +1.6%**. October’s cash invoice total is higher mostly because of a **€120k annual prepay from Gringotts** and a **duplicate Soylent invoice**.
- **Enterprise is the profit engine, but its margin is eroding.** Enterprise is **87% of October MRR** and **79% of October gross profit**. Yet Enterprise gross profit fell **€17.3k MoM** as infra + support costs rose **€17.8k**.
- **SMB has the clearest structural churn problem.** Four SMB Starter customers churned in October, representing **€123.6k ARR / €10.3k MRR**. SMB also has the highest support-ticket intensity relative to MRR.
- **Mid-market has a concentrated problem, not necessarily a segment-wide cut case.** Nakatomi churned (**€180k ARR / €15k MRR**), and Soylent is a serious risk: usage **-27%**, revenue down from **€22k to €19.5k**, and support tickets up from **3 to 8**, including a critical API-error ticket.
- **Acquisition cannot be judged by October attributed revenue alone.** Paid search looks strongest in October (**€238.8k attributed revenue**), but **€174k / 73%** is expansion credit for existing customers. Content is the most consistent new-logo channel; partner has the highest trial conversion but is lumpy and had no October paid-conversion rows.
- **CAC payback by channel cannot be calculated from this pack.** There is no channel spend data. Funnel “conversions” are paid trials, not paid customers, and trial-to-paid conversion is not tracked.
- **Plan priority: Enterprise deserves the next engineering focus** to protect margin, with a secondary Pro workstream for rate-limit/overage friction. Starter needs GTM/churn/support remediation, not the main engineering slot.

---

## 2. REVENUE & CUSTOMER HEALTH

### Headline revenue reconciliation

| Item | Sept 2026 | Oct 2026 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Subscription invoices as listed | €746.1k | €867.7k cash, or €757.7k MRR after annual normalization |
| Professional services | €51.0k | €5.7k |
| Total as listed | €797.1k | €892.9k |
| Less duplicate Soylent invoice | — | -€19.5k |
| Less Gringotts annual cash, add monthly equivalent | — | -€120.0k +€10.0k |
| **Deduplicated / normalized total** | **€797.1k** | **€763.4k** |

So:
- **Cash invoice total** rose from €797.1k to €892.9k as listed, but this is inflated.
- After deduplicating and normalizing the annual prepay, October is **€763.4k**, down **€33.7k / -4.2%** vs September.
- The decline is driven by professional services falling from **€51.0k to €5.7k**.
- Excluding one-time professional services, subscription MRR rose from **€746.1k to €757.7k**, up **€11.6k / +1.6%**.

### Segment MRR and forward view

Using customer/plan mapping:

| Segment | Sept MRR | Oct MRR | Oct churn MRR | Expansions effective next cycle | Forward MRR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Enterprise | €565.0k | €565.0k | €0 | +€16.5k | €581.5k |
| Mid-market | €142.0k | €142.5k | -€15.0k | +€1.5k | €129.0k |
| SMB | €39.1k | €50.2k | -€10.3k | €0 | €39.9k |
| **Total** | **€746.1k** | **€757.7k** | **-€25.3k** | **+€18.0k** | **€750.4k** |

Key implications:
- **Enterprise is growing forward** due to October expansion bookings at Stark, Umbrella, Globex, and Cyberdyne.
- **Mid-market is weakening forward** mainly because Nakatomi churned and Soylent is at risk.
- **SMB October MRR looks better than it is** because churned customers were still invoiced in October. Forward SMB MRR drops back to roughly September levels despite new logos.

### Churn

October churn:

| Customer | Segment | Plan | ARR | MRR | Churn date |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| Nakatomi | Mid-market | Pro | €180.0k | €15.0k | 2026-10-19 |
| Slate Rock | SMB | Starter | €24.0k | €2.0k | 2026-10-08 |
| Mega-lo-Mart | SMB | Starter | €32.4k | €2.7k | 2026-10-15 |
| Dinoco | SMB | Starter | €27.6k | €2.3k | 2026-10-22 |
| Buy-n-Large | SMB | Starter | €39.6k | €3.3k | 2026-10-27 |

Total churn: **€303.6k ARR / €25.3k MRR**.  
SMB churn alone: **€123.6k ARR / €10.3k MRR**.  
Mid-market churn: **€180.0k ARR / €15.0k MRR**.

### Usage and support signals

- Total requests rose from **31.04M to 31.51M**, up **+1.5%**.
- Excluding Acme, total requests rose from **26.84M to 29.20M**, up **+8.8%**.
- Acme requests fell **-45%**, from **4.20M to 2.31M**, but tokens only fell **-12%**. The operational note explains this as a shift from interactive API calls to two scheduled batch runs. This is not a demand-loss signal.
- Support tickets rose from **59 to 74**, up **+25.4%**.
- Soylent tickets rose from **3 to 8**.
- Wonka tickets rose from **4 to 7**, mostly rate-limit tickets.
- Stark remained high-ticket (**5 tickets**) and is over its Enterprise included request allowance.

## 3. ACQUISITION

### Funnel conversion rates

Funnel “conversions” are leads that reached a paid trial in the same month, not paid customers.

| Month | Channel | Leads | Trials | Trial rate |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Sept | Paid search | 520 | 44 | 8.5% |
| Sept | Content | 260 | 31 | 11.9% |
| Sept | Partner | 60 | 15 | 25.0% |
| Sept | Outbound | 160 | 10 | 6.3% |
| Oct | Paid search | 900 | 58 | 6.4% |
| Oct | Content | 330 | 34 | 10.3% |
| Oct | Partner | 75 | 17 | 22.7% |
| Oct | Outbound | 195 | 11 | 5.6% |

All channels saw trial conversion rates fall as lead volume rose. This suggests either diminishing returns or lower lead quality as spend/volume increased.

### Attributed revenue by channel

| Channel | Sept attributed revenue | Oct attributed revenue | Oct new-logo ARR | Oct expansion ARR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Paid search | €36.0k | €238.8k | €64.8k | €174.0k |
| Content | €45.6k | €63.6k | €45.6k | €18.0k |
| Partner | €166.8k | €0 | €0 | €0 |
| Outbound | €33.6k | €46.8k | €22.8k | €24.0k |
| **Total** | **€282.0k** | **€349.2k** | **€133.2k** | **€216.0k** |

Important caveats:
- Paid search’s October spike is **mostly expansion credit** for existing customers. That is not new customer acquisition.
- Content produced **€45.6k new-logo ARR** in both September and October, making it the most consistent new-logo channel in this dataset.
- Partner had the highest trial conversion rate but no October attributed revenue and only a small number of leads. It is lumpy and hard to scale based on this pack.
- Outbound remains low-conversion.

### CAC payback

**CAC payback by acquisition channel cannot be calculated reliably.**
Required inputs missing:
- channel spend;
- gross margin by channel/customer;
- retention or expansion assumptions;
- true trial-to-paid conversion timing.

The pack only provides leads, paid-trial counts, and marketing-platform attributed revenue. That is not enough for CAC payback.

## 4. PLAN ECONOMICS

All figures in €000s unless stated.

| Plan | Sept rev | Sept cost | Sept GP | Sept margin | Oct rev | Oct cost | Oct GP | Oct margin | Oct GP/customer | Oct tickets | Oct customers over included |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Enterprise | 659.0 | 447.0 | 212.0 | 32.2% | 659.5 | 464.8 | 194.7 | 29.5% | 13.9 | 35 | 2 / 14 |
| Pro | 63.0 | 20.5 | 42.5 | 67.5% | 66.2 | 24.7 | 41.5 | 62.7% | 4.6 | 28 | 3 / 9 |
| Starter | 24.1 | 15.7 | 8.4 | 34.9% | 32.0 | 21.7 | 10.3 | 32.2% | 0.8 | 11 | 0 / 13 |

Cost = infra + support. GP = revenue - cost.

### What stands out

- **Enterprise is by far the largest profit pool** but its gross profit fell **-€17.3k MoM**. Costs rose **€17.8k** while revenue was essentially flat.
- **Pro has the best margin** at **62.7%**, though margin fell from 67.5%. It has the highest overage/limit pressure: **3 of 9 Pro customers exceeded 600k included requests**.
- **Starter has the weakest unit economics**: only **€0.8k GP per customer** in October. It also had **4 of 13 October Starter customers churn**. Its support cost is **€10.3k**, equal to **32% of Starter revenue**.
- Forward plan MRR is important:
  - Enterprise: **€659.5k + €18.0k expansions = €677.5k**
  - Pro: **€66.2k - €15.0k Nakatomi churn = €51.2k**
  - Starter: **€32.0k - €10.3k SMB churn = €21.7k**

So Pro and Starter both face forward MRR declines, but Enterprise remains the dominant profit engine.

---

## 5. RECOMMENDATIONS

### Segment investment

- **Do not reduce investment in Enterprise.** It is stable/growing, has no October churn, and receives all October expansion bookings in this pack.
- If leadership insists on reducing investment in one segment, the data most supports **reducing SMB investment**, specifically high-churn Starter acquisition/support. SMB has:
  - **20.5% ARR churn** in October;
  - high support-ticket intensity;
  - very low ARR per customer.
- However, SMB new logos partly offset churn, so the right move is a **targeted reduction in high-churn SMB acquisition/support**, not cutting all SMB.
- **Mid-market does not look like a blanket cut case.** Its issue is concentrated in Nakatomi churn and Soylent risk. Treat it as an account-retention problem first.

### Acquisition spend

- **Do not increase paid search based on October attributed revenue alone.** Most of that revenue is expansion credit, not new-logo acquisition.
- The most defensible incremental test is **content**, because it produced consistent new-logo ARR in both months and has a trial conversion rate around 10–12%.
- **Partner** has the highest trial conversion, but it is lumpy and had no October paid-conversion rows. It could be a test candidate only with longer trial-to-paid tracking.
- Before scaling any channel, instrument spend by channel so CAC payback can actually be calculated.

### Product plan focus

- **Primary engineering focus: Enterprise.** It is 87% of MRR and 79% of gross profit, but its margin is falling. Reducing Enterprise infra/support cost has the largest financial leverage.
- **Secondary focus: Pro rate-limit/overage packaging.** Pro has the best margin, and 3 of 9 Pro customers exceed included requests. Many Pro support tickets are rate-limit related.
- **Starter needs GTM/churn/support remediation, not the main engineering priority.** Its revenue contribution is too small to justify the next quarter’s engineering focus unless the strategy is explicitly to fix SMB retention first.

### CFO request

- **CAC payback by acquisition channel is not calculable from this pack.** Provide interim attributed revenue and funnel conversion rates, but state clearly that spend data is required.

---

## 6. UNCERTAINTIES / DATA ISSUES

1. **Duplicate October invoice.** `INV-2026-10-0209` appears for Soylent from both `stripe` and `billing_sync`. Naive October revenue is overstated by **€19.5k**.
2. **Annual invoice normalization.** Gringotts’ **€120k annual subscription** is recorded as cash in October. Plans table treats it as **€10k/month**. Revenue comparisons must separate cash from MRR.
3. **Professional services are one-time.** September had **€51k**, October only **€5.7k**. This explains most of the normalized total revenue decline.
4. **Funnel conversions are paid trials, not paid customers.** Trial-to-paid conversion runs on a longer cycle and is not tracked in this pack.
5. **Acquisition attribution is not causal.** `attributed_revenue_eur` is what the marketing platform credited. It includes expansion bookings, and no spend data is provided.
6. **CAC payback cannot be calculated.** Missing channel spend, gross margin by channel, retention, and true conversion timing.
7. **Segment-level costs are not provided.** Plans table gives infra/support by plan, not by Enterprise / Mid-market / SMB. Segment profitability can only be approximated and should not be treated as precise.
8. **Plans table counts churned customers in the month.** October plan customers = 36, but active customers after October churn = 31.
9. **Usage change is distorted for Acme.** The **-45%** request drop is explained by the batch migration, not necessarily lost demand. Excluding Acme, requests grew **+8.8%**.
10. **New accounts have blank `usage_change_pct`.** Month-over-month usage trends cannot be calculated for them.
11. **Support cost allocation is plan-level.** `support_cost_eur` includes fully loaded CS staff assigned to the plan, so per-ticket or per-segment allocation is approximate.
